The FOMC statement is clearly positive—repeated “strong” descriptors, a rate hike, and “balanced” risks. SLOOS around this period corroborates the upbeat macro tone: banks (including foreign banks) reported easier C&I standards and narrower loan-rate spreads, frequently citing a better economic outlook and strong labor markets as reasons for easing. That accommodative credit supply alongside robust demand reinforces the case for normalization and slightly strengthens the bullish read—still not exuberant, but more constructive than before.
